newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean '96 CPI up 4.5 pct vs 4.7 pct rise in '95.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean '96 CPI up 4.5 pct vs 4.7 pct rise in '95.

text.p: South Korea's consumer price index (CPI) rose 4.5 percent in calendar 1996 against a 4.7 percent increase in 1995, figures from the Ministry of Finance and Economy showed on Sunday.
A ministry official said food prices rose 3.1 percent in 1996 while prices of non-food products grew 5.2 percent.

It said in a statement this year's CPI growth was in line with the government's target of capping this year's inflation at 4.5 percent. Strong efforts to stabilise consumer prices and good harvests helped achieve the target.
Prices of farm, fishery and forestry products rose by 1.8 percent in 1996, following a 0.2 percent drop in 1995.
Service charges remained the main factor pushing up overall consumer inflation, the statement said.
Charges for private services -- including restaurants and private education -- rose by 6.2 percent in 1996, following an 8.5 percent gain in 1995.
Public service charges, such as public transport fares and school fees, rose by 8.5 percent in 1996, the statement said.
The central Bank of Korea has forecast next year's CPI inflation at 4.7 percent.
